observations.title: ism-1657 / win-application-control-file-types — corp.example.gov.au/WKS-0044
observations.description: AppLocker enforces executables, installers, scripts, leaving libraries unrestricted. Separately: AppLocker has no rule collection for compiled HTML (.chm), HTML applications (.hta), control panel applets (.cpl), so these cannot be restricted by AppLocker however it is configured. App Control for Business (WDAC) covers more and is the route to this control.

relevant-evidence.description: Raw collected facts supporting this observation.

observations.title: ism-0843 / win-application-control-implemented — corp.example.gov.au/WKS-0044
observations.description: AppLocker is enforcing 3 rule collection(s): Exe, Msi, Script. Note that Dll is in AuditOnly mode and blocks nothing.

relevant-evidence.description: Raw collected facts supporting this observation.

observations.title: ism-1870 / win-application-control-user-writable-paths — corp.example.gov.au/WKS-0044
observations.description: Application control permits execution from 4 location/rule combination(s) that a non-administrator can write to, in the Exe, Script collection(s): a temporary folder used by the operating system (1 path(s), e.g. C:\Windows\Temp); a writable directory inside the Windows directory (1 path(s), e.g. C:\Windows\Tasks). Writing a file to one of these and running it is not blocked. Separately, 2 allow rule(s) scoped to administrative principals also cover these locations; those are recorded but not counted as a failure of this control.

relevant-evidence.description: Raw collected facts supporting this observation.
